raw_findings.message: Any row-parsing error silently stops loading the CSV, so a malformed row causes all following entries to be omitted from a report that still succeeds.
The output path is interpolated into a shell command, so a crafted `--out` value can execute arbitrary commands.
The optional units and repeatable groups accept empty or unitless durations; for example, `8` passes validation but is parsed as zero minutes.
A worker whose entries total zero minutes causes this division to raise `ZeroDivisionError` while rendering the report.
The first daily total is always skipped, so overtime on a worker's first recorded day is never counted.
Saturday has weekday value 5, so this condition counts Sunday but incorrectly excludes Saturday work from the weekend total.

raw_findings.message: Any malformed row causes loading to stop without an error, silently omitting that row and every later valid entry from the billing report.
The output path is interpolated into a shell command, so an attacker who controls `--out` can append shell metacharacters and execute arbitrary commands.
Optional units and repeated groups allow malformed values such as `8` or an empty string, which are silently parsed as zero minutes.
The repeated groups can partition long digit strings in exponentially many ways, so a long malformed duration can cause excessive backtracking and stall report generation.
A worker whose accepted entries total zero minutes causes `share_of_total` to divide by zero and abort report generation.
The first daily total is always skipped, so overtime on a worker's first recorded day is never counted.
`weekday()` returns 5 for Saturday, so the `> 5` condition excludes all Saturday work from the weekend total.

raw_findings.message: Any malformed row causes parsing to stop without an error, so later valid entries are omitted while the program reports success and produces an incomplete bill.
Using floating-point arithmetic for billing can produce inaccurate displayed amounts, such as $0.30000000000000004 for a $0.10 rate and three hours.
A quoted CSV worker value containing a newline is inserted directly into the report, allowing input to forge additional report lines or worker entries.
The output path is interpolated into a shell command with shell=True, so a crafted --out value can execute arbitrary commands.
The optional unit markers let malformed values such as "8" pass validation and parse as zero minutes, silently undercounting work.
A worker whose total is zero, for example from a zero-duration entry, causes report generation to crash when overtime share is calculated.
The first daily total is always skipped, so overtime on the first date encountered is never counted.
Saturday has weekday value 5, so the `> 5` check omits all Saturday work from the weekend total.
